title: Speculative prefetch and partial-success billing for vector ops and structured invocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We increasingly run speculative prefetches and parallel rerank/function calls for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, structured output). When speculative requests are started and only a subset succeed (partial success) or are de-duplicated downstream, current billing sometimes double-charges or attributes cost to the wrong logical request. Rate limiter quotas also don't account for speculative slots, which causes surprise rejections for bursty workloads.

Observed symptoms: intermittent billing reconciliation tickets, customer reports of unexpected token charges after client retries, and inconsistent per-route quota exhaustion when many speculative prefetches are active.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic accounting model that: (1) attributes costs for speculative and partial-success flows predictably, (2) updates rate-limiter and quota windows to represent speculative reservations without unfairly penalizing other traffic, and (3) provides clear audit events for reconciliation and customer support.
acceptance_criteria: Metering ledger emits atomic events for speculative attempts and finalizations (REQUEST_RESERVED, ATTEMPT_EXECUTED, PARTIAL_FINALIZED, FINALIZED, REFUNDED)

Billing must never charge final customer tokens > sum of confirmed successful token consumption for a logical request (allowing up to configurable speculative reservation cost that is explicitly visible)
Rate limiter exposes a speculative_budget parameter and prevents speculative slots from blocking guaranteed quota for non-speculative requests
All existing invoices remain numerically unchanged for non-speculative workloads (backwards compatibility), and a feature flag gates speculative-accounting rollout
End-to-end tests covering k-of-n success scenarios and idempotent retries pass in the CI metering harness
Dashboard surfaces speculative consumption and per-route partial_charge counts for 30d and 90d windows
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a lightweight reservation step: when a speculative prefetch or parallel call is spawned we emit a REQUEST_RESERVED ledger event with a small reservation token estimate and a speculative_parent_id. Reservation does not immediately finalize billing but reduces a new speculative_budget counter in the rate limiter.

2) On execution completion we emit ATTEMPT_EXECUTED with observed tokens. For successful attempts we write PARTIAL_FINALIZED entries that link to the speculative_parent_id. A final reconciliation job aggregates PARTIAL_FINALIZED rows for the parent and emits a FINALIZED event that contains the canonical charged tokens. If the parent is aborted/cancelled we emit REFUNDED events to release reservation counters and produce refund ledger rows.

3) Update rate limiter to maintain two counters per key: guaranteed_quota and speculative_budget. Guaranteed_quota is consumed first. Speculative_budget is optional and shrinkable (configurable per-route and per-tenant). If speculative_budget is exhausted, speculative requests are rejected with 429+X-Speculative-Info header.

4) Use idempotency keys and speculative_parent_id to dedupe duplicate attempts and to make reconciliation deterministic. The reconciliation job is run synchronously when possible for single-parent flows and as a background aggregator for large k-of-n flows.

5) Add telemetry: billing.reservation_attempts, billing.partial_insufficient_refunds, billing.final_charged_tokens, rate_limit.speculative_rejections. Expose these in the Console billing view and per-route dashboards.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity: adds an extra ledger event type and reconciliation worker, increasing operational surface.
- Latency: trying to reconcile synchronously for some flows may add a small delay before final invoiceable amount is available; we mitigate by finalizing asynchronously in most cases and surfacing interim reservation info.
- UX: customers will see 'reserved' consumption that can change; we will surface reservation and finalization clearly in the Console to reduce confusion.

Rationale: the deterministic reconciliation prevents surprise double-billing and allows speculative performance optimizations without permanently charging failed attempts. The speculative_budget ensures fair sharing across tenants while preserving burst capability for models requiring prefetching.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (feature-flagged, internal tenants only): implement ledger events + reconciliation worker + rate-limiter speculative_budget. Deploy to canary and observe metrics for 2 weeks.

Phase 2 (beta customers): enable for selected customers with opt-in toggle in Console and monitor billing differences and support tickets for 4 weeks. Run automated refund-script for any mischarges found during beta.

Phase 3 (default opt-in): enable for all hosted customers and document behavior. For Dedicated/Private, document configuration knobs and provide migration guide.

All phases include a migration script to normalize historical speculative reservations to ledger rows so dashboards can be computed consistently.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Emit the following metrics and set alert thresholds: billing.partial_finalized_rate > 5% of attempts (P2), billing.refund_rate spike > 0.5% (P1), rate_limit.speculative_rejections increase > 3x baseline (P1).

Create dashboard panels: per-tenant speculative_budget usage, speculative vs final charged tokens, and reconciliation job latency and error rate. Add automated daily sanity-check job that validates sum(FINALIZED.tokens) == sum(partial_finalized.tokens aggregated) for processed parents.
test_plan:
Unit tests for ledger event creation and idempotency key handling. Integration tests in metering-harness that simulate: single success, k-of-n success (e.g., 2-of-5), full failure, client retry with same idempotency key, and duplicate speculative attempts. Load test that exercises speculative_budget exhaustion and validates 429 semantics. End-to-end billing regression tests to ensure vanilla non-speculative flows produce identical invoices.

Post-deploy smoke tests: run a synthetic customer workload to verify billing metrics and refund paths for aborted parents.
